sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.
Heard learned advocate Mr.Kuldip Acharya appearing on behalf of the applicant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor Ms.Vrunda Shah appearing on behalf of the respondent-State.
2. Rule. Learned APP waives service of rule on behalf of the respondent-State.

3. The applicant has filed this application under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for enlarging the applicant on Regular Bail in connection with FIR being C.R. No.

sentences.text: Learned advocate for the applicant would submit that considering the role attributed to the applicant, and nature of the allegation levelled, the applicant may be enlarged on regular bail.
It is further submitted that since the charge- sheet is filed no useful purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in jail for indefinite period.
It is further contended that the applicant is ready and willing to abide by all the conditions that may be imposed by this Court if released on bail.
5. As against the same, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent - State has vehemently objected to the grant of regular bail.

Learned APP has submitted that looking to the nature of offence and the role attributed to the present applicant as coming out from the charge-sheet, this Court may not exercise the discretion in favour of the applicant and the application may be dismissed.
6. I have heard learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers.

Following NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/6976/2026 ORDER DATED: 27/03/2026 undefined aspects are considered:-
i.

While the present FIR inter alia alleges that the applicant, being a Chairman and Managing Director of a company, had lured investors with high returns and after having taken investments from the complainant and other victims, had not given the returns as promised and had defrauded the complainant and other victims.
ii. While the FIR states as regards an amount defrauded being Rs.15,04,820/- post investigation it appears that the amount has increased to approximately rupees two and a half crores.

iii. Again, it would appear that the present is not the only offence against the present applicant, it would appear that the present applicant has been arraigned as a accused in 62 other FIRs where the allegations are selfsame as described above.

iv. Having noted as above, this Court has also considered the fact that the present applicant has been arrested in connection with the present offence on 06.11.2018 and the charge-sheet has been filed.

v. This Court has also noticed the order of the Hon'ble NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/6976/2026 ORDER DATED: 27/03/2026 undefined Apex Court in Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 394/2024 dated 19.05.2025 whereby the Hon'ble Apex Court has inter alia directed clubbing of FIRs against the present applicant State wise and whereas, insofar as the Gujarat State is concerned, while there are four FIRs registered against the present applicant, the preset FIR is directed to be treated as the lead FIR and whereas, the other three FIRs are directed to be clubbed along with the same.

vi. This Court has also considered the fact that the Hon'ble Supreme Court at para-20 has inter alia observed that if the applicant has been granted bail in connection with the proceedings / criminal case to which other cases have been clubbed, the bail so granted must enure to the petitioner's favour in Ravindrasingh Avatarsingh Sindhu vs State Of Gujarat on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178504311/
2 other FIRs clubbed along with the principal FIR. vii.

sentences.text:
Having noticed as above, it would appear that while the present is the principal FIR, with which the FIRs have been clubbed, yet, in other FIRs i.e.
the FIRs filed in the Ahmedabad City, two in number, the applicant has been enlarged on bail by the learned Sessions Court vide orders dated 03.04.2023.

viii. Having regard to the period of incarceration undergone NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/6976/2026 ORDER DATED: 27/03/2026 undefined i.e. approximately 8 years and also considering the fact that in the FIRs which are clubbed with the present FIR, which is treated as the principal FIR, the present applicant has been enlarged on regular bail and also considering the fact that granting regular bail to the present applicant may not result in the present applicant being enlarged since the bail has been dismissed in large number of cases, this Court is inclined to allow this application.
This Court has taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40.
7.

In the facts and circumstances of the case and considering the nature of the allegations made against the applicant in the First Information Report, without discussing the evidence in detail,
prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that this is a fit case to exercise the discretion and enlarge the applicant on regular bail.
8. Hence, the present application is allowed.

9. The Authorities will release the applicant only if he is not required in connection with any other offence for the time being.

If breach of any of the above conditions is committed, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/6976/2026 ORDER DATED: 27/03/2026 undefined the Sessions Court concerned will be free to take appropriate action in the matter.
